assessments.reasoning: The retained Lua 5.4 manual identifies the collector as Lua's automatic memory-management mechanism and explicitly includes both strings and tables. It relates collection to whether objects remain accessible and allows finalizers to make a dead object accessible again.

challenge.method: Check whether dropping a local reference guarantees immediate reclamation, including when the registry still holds the object.
challenge.results: A registry reference keeps the object accessible. Even for an inaccessible object, the manual promises eventual collection without a deadline. The passage concerns memory managed by Lua.

limitations: The rule concerns Lua-managed memory and gives no fixed collection time. The manual qualifies reachability and finalization.
The finding covers the documented Lua-managed objects. It supplies no deadline or guarantee about separately managed host memory.
